elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.1 retained: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." plus "The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims." No unlimited-Customer-liability language remains.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered 21.1: "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000." Basis is fees paid or payable (not broader "all amounts"), the 12-month lookback is anchored exactly as in the playbook's model language, and the USD 1,000,000 floor is present. The deterministic "lookback precedes the claim" miss is a literal string artefact: "preceding the event giving rise to the claim" is the anchor the model language itself prescribes. Use of lowercase "fees" with the express scope "under this Agreement and all Order Forms" displaces the illusory defined "Fees" (Implementation Fee, USD 12,000), and in any event the greater-of floor makes the cap no less than USD 1,000,000.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.2 (unchanged): "Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill..." — bilateral by its terms.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims includes "a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations", and 21.1/21.2 both open "Except for Excluded Claims", so these sit outside the cap.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3: "breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations" within Excluded Claims, which are excepted from the 21.1 cap.
21.3: "its indemnification obligations" listed in Excluded Claims; 21.1 cap applies "Except for Excluded Claims".
21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" within Excluded Claims.
21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" within Excluded Claims.
21.3: "...or fraud" within Excluded Claims, excepted from the cap in 21.1.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" within Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Rendered 21.3: "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed amounts due for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section." The edit replaces the illusory noun "Fees" (USD 12,000 Implementation Fee) with "amounts due", so the carve-out now reaches Customer's payment obligations generally rather than a narrow defined subset. The retained qualifiers "undisputed" and "for conforming Services" describe the payment obligation itself (Customer has no obligation to pay disputed or non-conforming charges) and are Customer-favourable retained language that could not be deleted without a minimality failure; the deterministic miss is a string artefact of searching for the noun "Fees"/"payment obligations".

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.1: "each Party's total aggregate liability... The cap is mutual...".

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: 21.1 as amended: fees paid or payable "during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim", with a USD 1,000,000 floor; scope broadened to "this Agreement and all Order Forms", curing the sub-six-months illusory basis.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims: "breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations".

reasons: Deviation classification is correct: as drafted, the cap was measured by "Fees" defined as a one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form only, which is far below six months' fees and therefore walk-away territory, and the payment carve-out was keyed to the same illusory noun.

The preferred checklist is complete on the rendered operative language: mutual cap, greater-of 12-months-fees / USD 1,000,000 basis, mutual indirect-damages exclusion, all seven preferred carve-outs already in the Excluded Claims definition (which both 21.1 and 21.2 except), and a payment carve-out now keyed to "amounts due" rather than the narrow defined "Fees".

Both deterministic misses are string artefacts rather than substantive defects: the lookback "preceding the event giving rise to the claim" is precisely the anchor used in the playbook's own model language, and the payment carve-out now uses "amounts due" (the regex looked for "Fees"/"payment obligations").

Minimality holds: only two operations — the cap basis/floor and the payment-carve-out noun — with no survival tail, no added damages categories, no procedures, and no deletion of favourable retained wording ("undisputed", "for conforming Services", the mutuality sentence, and the direct-damages sentence in 21.2 all survive).

Intent is preserved: no dangling cross-references, and no retained sentence contradicts the amended cap. One residual drafting risk worth raising in negotiation (not an element failure): clause 1.5 still defines "Fees" as the Implementation Fee while 21.1 now uses lowercase "fees". The express scope "under this Agreement and all Order Forms" and the USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor mean the cap cannot fall below USD 1,000,000 in any reading, but the drafter may wish to say "all fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and any Order Form (regardless of the definition of \"Fees\")" to remove any argument that the defined term applies.
Comment tone and content comply: it states the playbook position, explains the illusory "Fees" basis, and confirms indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.
